walkthroughs.body_html:
Financial Information and Decisions — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Financial Information and Decisions brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Financial Information and Decisions.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Schumpeter described entrepreneurs as agents of:
options: Marginal utility
Creative destruction
Comparative advantage
Perfect competition

mcqs.q: Roughly what percentage of UK start-ups fail within three years?

options: PESTLE analyses the internal strengths and weaknesses of a business.
PESTLE stands for Profit, Earnings, Sales, Trade, Loans, Equity.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
The external macro-environment: Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors affecting a business.
Shareholders' personal assets are protected if the company fails — they can only lose the amount they invested, not their personal wealth.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Limited liability means the company has limited debts it can take on.
Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.

mcqs.q: What is operations management concerned with?
options: Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.
Limited liability means a business can only operate for a limited time.
Operations management is the same as general management.
The design and control of the production process and business operations — converting inputs into outputs efficiently. It includes capacity, quality, supply chain, and process improvement.
